name: Cryptic crossword No 29,863
preamble: An earlier version of this puzzle was published in error.

clue.text: Unsophisticated port found in pub and clubs

indicators.note: something found in a place sits inside it, so one piece is placed within the others

blocks.note: a bar is a pub
Bari is a port in southern Italy
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: A rough harbour town whose drinkers spill between the pub and the nightclubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' is not the drink you might order in a pub but a town: Bari, on Italy's Adriatic coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbaric behaviour is crude and uncultured, the opposite of refined or civilised manners.

clue.text: Weapon stored in rack at an armoury

indicators.note: goods stored in a place are kept inside it, so the letters lie within the phrase that follows

blocks.note: runs across the end of rack, all of at and an, and the start of armoury

explanation.surface: A blade kept on a rack in an arsenal, exactly where weapons belong.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer spans four words: racK AT AN Armoury.
explanation.definitionFit: A katana is the long curved sword traditionally carried by Japanese samurai warriors.

clue.text: Commercial opening some time in December

blocks.note: an ad is a commercial
a vent is an opening or outlet

explanation.surface: A shop or advert launching sometime in December, ready for the festive season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commercial opening' reads as a shop launch; split it into two separate nouns.
explanation.definitionFit: Advent is the church season of preparation before Christmas, covering most of December.

clue.text: Southern British artist, completely, endlessly influential

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
Tracey Emin is a British artist
all means completely; its last letter goes

explanation.surface: Praise for a southern British artist as wholly and endlessly influential.
explanation.walkthrough: Tracey Emin is a well-known British artist, famous for 'My Bed'. ALL, completely, loses its end to give AL.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminal work strongly shapes later developments, like a seed from which others grow.

clue.text: Remote institute scheduled to receive nothing

indicators.note: receiving something means taking it in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: I is the abbreviation for institute
slated means scheduled, as in slated for next week
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An outlying institute is scheduled to get no funding at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The O sits inside SLATED, after the opening I.
explanation.definitionFit: An isolated place is far away and cut off from others, just like a remote one.

clue.text: Nice, redeveloped street around the outskirts of Ashington is Northumberland’s best

indicators.note: something redeveloped is rebuilt in a new form, so these letters are rearranged
the outskirts are the edges, so only the outer letters are kept
going around something encloses it, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: the French city name, taken as letters to rearrange
first and last letters of the town name
ST is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Ashington, a town in Northumberland, gets a smart redeveloped street that locals call the area's finest.
explanation.walkthrough: Nice is the French city, not the adjective. Canny is northern English dialect for good or nice, used heavily in Northumberland.
explanation.definitionFit: In Northumbrian and Geordie speech canny means good or pleasant, so the superlative form serves as the local word for finest.

clue.text: Rip off winter clothing

blocks.note: first meaning: to swindle or overcharge someone
second meaning: a warm jacket of soft synthetic fabric

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like tearing off a warm coat; the two phrases are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for cheating someone of money and a noun for a cosy fluffy jacket worn in cold weather.

clue.text: Second fantastically safe and natural feature of California

indicators.note: something done fantastically is wildly unreal, so the letters are freely rearranged

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
all fourteen letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Praise for Californian living as both very safe and wholesomely natural.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' looks like a link but is part of the letter mix. The irony is that the answer is the earthquake zone, hardly safe.
explanation.definitionFit: The San Andreas Fault is the great geological fracture running through California, a landform in the strict sense.

clue.text: Scrape some cedar bark back

indicators.note: some of a phrase is only part of it, so the letters lie within the words
going back means running the opposite way, so the letters are read right to left

blocks.note: the string runs from inside cedar into the start of bark

explanation.surface: Instructions to scrape off a bit of cedar bark and put it back.
explanation.walkthrough: Read cEDAR BArk from right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: To abrade is to wear away a surface by rubbing or grinding, which is scraping.

clue.text: I speak badly of Robinson Crusoe, for example

blocks.note: taken as written
to slander is to speak badly of someone

explanation.surface: Someone confessing to bad-mouthing the famous castaway.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'I' is just the letter I, with the verb phrase following it.
explanation.definitionFit: Crusoe lived for years on a desert island, so he is one example of someone who lives on an island.

clue.text: Mum’s heading inside to make a meal

indicators.note: the heading sits at the top, so only the first letter is kept
going inside something means being enclosed within it

blocks.note: first letter of Mum
to create is to make
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mum heads into the kitchen to cook up something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To make a' looks like a link to the definition but is wordplay. A cream tea is a British afternoon snack of tea with scones, jam and clotted cream.
explanation.definitionFit: A cream tea is a light afternoon repast of scones, jam, clotted cream and a pot of tea.

clue.text: Popular surfing location in those days ultimately became old-hat

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only final letters are kept

blocks.note: then means at that time, in those days
last letters of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A once-fashionable surf beach whose popularity faded and became dated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surfing' is web browsing, not riding waves, so the location is online.
explanation.definitionFit: People surf the internet, browsing from page to page, so the web is a place where surfing happens.

clue.text: Untidy spot packed with rubbish

indicators.note: a thing packed with something holds it inside

blocks.note: to spot is to spy
crap is slang for rubbish

explanation.surface: A messy place stuffed full of junk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot' reads as a noun, a place, but works as the verb, to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scrappy is disorganised and messy, put together in bits rather than neatly.

clue.text: Fancy loafers featuring stitching in the middle or outside

indicators.note: fancy here means elaborately reworked, so the letters are rearranged
the middle is the centre, so only the central letter is kept

blocks.note: the shoe name, taken as letters
the central letter of a nine-letter word

explanation.surface: Designer slip-on shoes with stitching in the centre or around the edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy loafers' reads as smart shoes, and 'outside' seems to describe stitching, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Al fresco is an Italian-derived phrase meaning in the open air, as in dining under the sky.

clue.text: Most courteous people in the US regularly ignored it in the end

indicators.note: ignoring at regular intervals drops every other letter, keeping the rest
the end is the final position, so only the last letter is kept

blocks.note: first, third, fifth letters and so on
last letter of it

explanation.surface: The best-mannered Americans were routinely snubbed in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'People in the US' looks like it wants Americans; instead take every other letter of those four words.
explanation.definitionFit: Polite means courteous, and the superlative form marks the highest degree of good manners.

clue.text: Extraordinarily storied journos

indicators.note: something extraordinary is out of the ordinary, so the letters leave their usual order

blocks.note: taken as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Journalists with remarkably colourful, legendary careers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Storied' is fodder, though it fits journalists' stories nicely.
explanation.definitionFit: Journo is informal slang for a journalist, and newspaper editors are senior journalists.

clue.text: Type of music that is superlatively fast

blocks.note: rap is a genre of music
id est is the Latin for that is, abbreviated i.e.

explanation.surface: A musical genre described as the quickest of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That is' looks like a link phrase, but it gives the Latin ID EST.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid means quick, so its superlative names the very quickest; 'superlatively' signals the -est ending.

clue.text: Promising young actor is extremely likeable in debut

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only the outer letters are kept
placed in something means set inside it

blocks.note: a debut is a start
first and last letters

explanation.surface: A rising young performer comes across as very charming in a first film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Debut' reads as an actor's first role, but it simply means a beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: A starlet is a young actress tipped for future stardom, an up-and-coming performer.

clue.text: Scared to ignore the first load of gossip?

indicators.note: ignoring the first means leaving off the opening letter

blocks.note: fearful means scared; it loses its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone too frightened to brush off the leading rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: FEARFUL without its F.
explanation.definitionFit: To get an earful is to be told a great deal, often gossip or a scolding, filling the ears.

clue.text: Reddish brown and gold glow

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
to burn is to glow with heat or light

explanation.surface: Describing the warm red-brown and golden shimmer of hair or autumn leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reddish brown and gold' reads as a list of colours; only the first two words define.
explanation.definitionFit: Auburn is the colour name for hair of a warm reddish-brown shade.

clue.text: Intricate pattern covering tip of sunbittern’s wing

indicators.note: something intricate is intertwined and complex, so the letters are rearranged
a tip is a point at one end, here the start, so only the first letter is kept
covering something means wrapping over it, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: taken as letters to rearrange
first letter of the bird's name

explanation.surface: Describing the intricate markings on a sunbittern's wing, a South American bird with striking wing patterns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wing' is not the bird's but a church's. The sunbittern really does flash an elaborate eyespot pattern when it spreads its wings.
explanation.definitionFit: A transept is one of the two arms crossing the nave of a cross-shaped church, a side wing of the building.

clue.text: Fix all the taps and central heating to begin with

indicators.note: to begin with means at the start, so only first letters are kept

blocks.clueFragment: all the taps and central heating
blocks.note: first letter of each of the six words

explanation.surface: A plumber's job list: repair every tap and the boiler first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fix' reads as repair, but here it means fasten.
explanation.definitionFit: To fix something in place is to fasten or join it to something else.

clue.text: Short episodic story about European football league

indicators.note: something cut short has lost its end, so the last letter is dropped
about means around, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: a serial is a story told in episodes, missing its last letter
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A brief serialised tale about a continental soccer competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European' looks like it describes the league, but it only supplies E. Serie A is Italy's top professional football division.
explanation.definitionFit: Serie A is the name of the top division of Italian professional football, a national league.

clue.text: Aim finally to bother someone who protests

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so only last letters are kept

blocks.note: an object is an aim or goal
last letters of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A protester whose eventual goal is to annoy people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' applies to both following words, giving O and R.
explanation.definitionFit: An objector raises objections, voicing disagreement or opposition to something.

clue.text: Vehement rant from one stuck in traffic

indicators.note: something stuck in a thing is lodged inside it

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to traffic is to trade, especially illicitly

explanation.surface: A driver stuck in a jam bursts into a furious rant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Traffic' means commerce, not cars on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A tirade is a long angry speech of criticism or denunciation, a furious outburst.

clue.text: Seed crops mixed with something corny and dairy product

indicators.note: things mixed are stirred together, so the letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: taken as letters to rearrange
cheese is anything trite or sentimental, hence cheesy

explanation.surface: A farming scene: grain crops blended with sweetcorn and milk products.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corny' suggests corn on the farm, but it means sentimental and trite, which is cheesy.
explanation.definitionFit: Processed cheese is a factory-made cheese product, sold in slices or tubs, made from milk.
